# Palbase

> Palbase — the backend for apps. Every project has auth, storage, realtime,
> flags, notifications, secrets, analytics, AI and purchases, called from web
> apps with the publishable key (`palbase/web`), from iOS (Swift) and Android
> (Kotlin) with the native SDKs, and from servers with the secret key
> (`palbase/server`). Your own backend runs on a machine built from a GitHub
> branch on every push, beside a Postgres database of its own. Backends are
> `palbase/backend`: `@Controller` classes whose methods are routes,
> `@Injectable` services that arrive by constructor, a `@Module` that lists what
> exists, `PalbaseFactory.create(AppModule)` in `src/main.ts`, and the schema
> declared with Palgres in `src/db/public.ts`. A push to the branch is the
> deploy; the CLI (`npx palbase`) does the rest — client apps, the purchase
> catalog, environments, tokens.

## Getting Started

- [Introduction](https://palbase.studio/docs/getting-started/introduction): What Palbase is: the modules every project has — auth, storage, realtime, flags, notify, secrets, analytics, ai — and the machines and databases that run your own code.
- [Quickstart](https://palbase.studio/docs/getting-started/quickstart): Create a project in Studio, sign a user in from a web app, then put a backend on a machine from GitHub and call it.
- [Organizations](https://palbase.studio/docs/getting-started/organizations): Organizations, projects and environments; members, invitations and the owner, admin and member roles; your Studio account's security; and the organization's audit log.
- [Architecture](https://palbase.studio/docs/getting-started/architecture): How a palbase/backend app is shaped: a root module and one module per domain, thin controllers, services that arrive by constructor, schemas beside them, and the database declared in db/.
- [Project Structure](https://palbase.studio/docs/getting-started/project-structure): How a backend repository is laid out for a machine: src/main.ts, src/modules/<domain>/, src/db/, its Dockerfile, .env.example and tsconfig.json.
- [Access Tokens](https://palbase.studio/docs/getting-started/access-tokens): Organization access tokens for CI and agents: PALBASE_TOKEN, the member and admin roles, what a token cannot do, expiry, and deleting one.
- [Billing](https://palbase.studio/docs/getting-started/billing): The Free plan and Pay as you go: opening the organization's payment account, top-ups, what is charged, each environment's cap, Free and freeze, what happens when the balance runs out, and the billing API.
- [Usage & Limits](https://palbase.studio/docs/getting-started/usage-and-limits): What is metered for each environment and where Studio shows it, the rates and monthly limits it runs under, what a free project gets, and what each limit answers.
- [Logs](https://palbase.studio/docs/getting-started/logs): Studio's Logs by category: every request to the environment's address, auth's events, notifications, machine output and builds — and the request lines read from a server.

## CLI

- [Overview](https://palbase.studio/docs/cli/overview): palbase, the CLI in the npm package: signing in, choosing an environment, running a backend on your computer, tokens for CI and for AI agents, asking Palbase's support line, and what its commands cover.
- [Reference](https://palbase.studio/docs/cli/reference): Every command of the palbase CLI with its usage, what it does and its flags, as the CLI's own help prints them.

## Backend SDK

- [Overview](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/overview): palbase/backend — the framework your machine runs: PalbaseFactory, modules, class controllers, and the three things a handler imports — Palbase, Database and Log.
- [Modules & Dependency Injection](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/modules): @Module's four lists, @Injectable providers, injection by constructor type, onStart and onShutdown, and the mistakes refused at boot by name.
- [Controllers & Routing](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/controllers): @Controller classes, the HTTP method decorators, route options (auth, rateLimit, transaction), path parameters, @Resolve — parameters the app makes — and what a handler's return becomes, a Response included.
- [Request Validation](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/validation): @Body, @QueryParams, @Param and @Headers with any Standard Schema — zod, valibot, arktype — and the 400 a failed one answers.
- [Authentication](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/authentication): Secure-by-default routes, @User and @OptionalUser, verified email, test users, and how a caller's token is checked.
- [Responses & Errors](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/errors): What a handler's answer becomes, the error envelope, the built-in error classes and PalError, and what an outage or a crash answers.
- [Database](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/database): Database — the request's own transaction: typed tables, raw SQL with $query, plans with $transaction, $atomic and $asService().
- [Schema](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/schema): Your Postgres schema in TypeScript with defineSchema, defineTable, column builders, indexes, foreign keys and raw units.
- [Row-Level Security](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/row-level-security): Policies in the schema DSL, auth.uid(), the anon and authenticated roles, and $asService() for what the service does.
- [Field Encryption](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/encryption): text().encrypted(): a column sealed by your app with the project's keys — equality through a lookup, rows encrypted beside the serving release, key rotation, Studio's mask, and palbase/server's fields for any other server.
- [Encrypted Requests](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/request-encryption): encrypted() and encrypt(): a field the app seals before the request leaves the device and opens in the answer — keys and rotation, the errors, machines:call and Try it, and palbase/server's transit for any other server.
- [Schema changes](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/migrations): There are no migration files: a release migrates beside the version that serves — start, rollout, complete — with renamedFrom, fillWith and ignored for the changes that need them.
- [Storage](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/storage): Palbase.storage — buckets, objects, public reads, signed URLs and image renditions, from your backend.
- [Direct Uploads](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/direct-uploads): Files straight to storage: signed upload URLs your backend grants, and @Upload routes — storage asks the route where a file goes, then runs it with the stored object.
- [Secrets](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/secrets): The project's secrets: the set a machine is started with, and Palbase.secrets for values read while it runs.
- [Flags](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/flags): Palbase.flags — define flags, give single users their own values, and read what a user sees, from your backend.
- [Notifications](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/notifications): Palbase.notify — email, push, SMS and WhatsApp, templates, topics, each user's preferences, when a message goes (their own hour, quiet hours, the marketing cap), audiences, İYS and stop texts.
- [Journeys](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/journeys): Messages, waits, branches and A/B splits a person goes through after what they did: the definition, Studio's flow editor and templates, a try on a test user, publishing, the report and journey.* events.
- [Realtime](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/realtime): Palbase.realtime — broadcast to a channel's subscribers and write its shared state from your backend.
- [Gateways](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/gateways): @Gateway — a realtime channel of the app: who may join, typed events, members' messages and their acks, the channel's moments, durable gateways that keep what they send, and pipes.
- [Channels](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/channels): The realtime module's own channel declaration, for a backend that is not a palbase/backend app: who may join, publish and write state.
- [AI](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/ai): Palbase.ai — one-shot answers, tools that run on your machine, agents defined at each turn, and chats your backend starts, which their members reach through a gateway.
- [Webhooks](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/webhooks): @Webhook — a third party's deliveries (Stripe, GitHub, Slack, …) at POST /webhooks/<name>, each signature checked before an @On of its event runs.
- [Event Hooks](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/hooks): @On — handle the platform's events (user.deleted, file.uploaded, …) in your backend, each delivery signed and run once.
- [Cron](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/cron): @Cron — a provider the platform runs on a schedule (five fields of cron's, on a time zone's clocks), waking the machine for it; run now, paused and resumed from Studio and the CLI.
- [Tasks](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/tasks): @Task and Tasks.enqueue — work put on the machine's queue, done once, now or later: made again when it fails, failed tasks kept to try again, the machine asleep in between.
- [Cache](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/cache): Cache — the project's short-lived entries, shared by every copy of a machine: get, set, getOrSet, incr and del, time to live, the quota, and what a call does when the cache is away.
- [Translations](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/translations): t() — a sentence in the caller's language: palbase/strings/ kept with the code by `palbase strings`, missing translations from your AI module with --translate.
- [Test Users](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/test-users): Test users made with the secret key: what marks them, how to make and remove them, and user.test in a route.
- [Testing](https://palbase.studio/docs/backend/testing): Testing a backend: services as plain classes, and the app's whole HTTP layer through handle(), with no network.

## Web SDK

- [Overview](https://palbase.studio/docs/web/overview): palbase/web — createClient with the project's address and publishable key: what the client holds (auth, flags, analytics, consent, notify, purchases, the socket, your backend), its entry points, and what the project answers a browser.
- [Auth](https://palbase.studio/docs/web/auth): Sign-up, sign-in, sessions, second factors, passkeys, magic links and phone codes in the browser.
- [Calling Your Backend](https://palbase.studio/docs/web/backend-calls): pb.<backend> — your machine's routes as typed calls from the module palbase apps:sync writes, the Vite plugin that builds each environment, BackendError, and CORS.
- [Error Handling](https://palbase.studio/docs/web/errors): PalbaseError — status, code, request id and Retry-After — the retries the client makes, and the ones it never makes.
- [Uploads](https://palbase.studio/docs/web/uploads): Sending a file from the browser to storage: to your backend's upload route, or to a signed upload URL your backend made.
- [Flags](https://palbase.studio/docs/web/flags): pb.flags — the project's flags and remote configuration for this reader, read without the network, kept current over realtime, with experiments' exposures.
- [Realtime](https://palbase.studio/docs/web/realtime): Channels over the project's one socket: join, listen to broadcasts, leave — and who may join what.
- [Messaging](https://palbase.studio/docs/web/messaging): pb.messaging — the person's conversations kept in IndexedDB and current over the socket: lists, timelines and threads to subscribe to, an outbox that sends once, files encrypted in the browser, and onIncoming for the page's own banner.
- [Gateways](https://palbase.studio/docs/web/gateways): Your backend's gateways from the generated module: join, typed events, messages and their acks, GatewayError's reasons, durable history, and a chat gateway's state.
- [Analytics](https://palbase.studio/docs/web/analytics): pb.analytics — events, page views, person properties and the browser's own measures, held to the person's consent — and the people, places and audiences the project reads back.
- [Consent](https://palbase.studio/docs/web/consent): pb.consent — what the person allowed, key by key: the platform's keys, starting values, a consent screen, Global Privacy Control, and the calls under it.
- [Notifications](https://palbase.studio/docs/web/notifications): pb.notify — web push and its service worker, the signed-in person's inbox drawn ready, in-app messages shown in the page, and their preferences and topics.
- [Next.js](https://palbase.studio/docs/web/nextjs): Next.js: palbase/web/ssr keeps the session in a cookie the browser and your server both read — the proxy, server components, route handlers — and palbase/server acts as the project.

## iOS SDK

- [Overview](https://palbase.studio/docs/ios/overview): The iOS SDK in Swift: palbase-swift with Swift Package Manager, its products, iOS 18, registering the app, apps:sync and the Xcode build rule that compiles an environment in, PalbaseClient, the session in the keychain, errors and retries.
- [Auth](https://palbase.studio/docs/ios/auth): pb.auth in Swift: the observable sign-in state, email and password, guests, passkeys, Sign in with Apple and Google, second factors, magic links, phone codes, passwords and the user's sessions.
- [Calling Your Backend](https://palbase.studio/docs/ios/backend-calls): The typed Swift client apps:sync generates for your backend: pb.<name>, request and response types, typed errors, BackendError, file uploads and untyped calls.
- [Gateways](https://palbase.studio/docs/ios/gateways): Your backend's gateways from Swift: join, the Event, Send and Reply enums, PBGatewayError's reasons, durable history, and a chat gateway's PBChat for SwiftUI.
- [Realtime](https://palbase.studio/docs/ios/realtime): pb.realtime: channels on the project's one socket, broadcasts, the state every member shares, presence, who may join, and the socket's observable status.
- [Messaging](https://palbase.studio/docs/ios/messaging): PalbaseMessaging: @Observable conversations, timelines and threads, an outbox that sends once, incoming() for the app's own banner, and the notification service extension that brings a message onto the phone while the app is closed.
- [Flags](https://palbase.studio/docs/ios/flags): pb.flags: feature flags read without waiting, observable in SwiftUI, kept current over realtime, a signed-in user's values, and experiments' $flag_exposure.
- [Analytics](https://palbase.studio/docs/ios/analytics): pb.analytics: events, screens, the person's properties, the app's own events such as $install and $app_open, timings, diagnostics, and App Tracking Transparency.
- [Consent](https://palbase.studio/docs/ios/consent): pb.consent: the platform's keys and the app's own, starting values, the person's choices, region and needsAsking, and whose the choices are across sign-in and sign-out.
- [Notifications](https://palbase.studio/docs/ios/notifications): pb.notify: APNs registration and push reports, preferences and topics, the notification service extension, the inbox, and in-app messages drawn in SwiftUI.
- [Storage](https://palbase.studio/docs/ios/storage): pb.storage: uploading and downloading at URLs your backend signs, a public bucket's objects, and what an upload answers.
- [Purchases](https://palbase.studio/docs/ios/purchases): pb.purchases: what the customer has in any store, buying and restoring in the App Store, the published paywall drawn in SwiftUI, offers and codes, and web checkout from the app.
- [Voice](https://palbase.studio/docs/ios/voice): PBVoice from palbase-swift-voice: a chat's live voice over WebRTC, its offer through your backend, the audio session, muting and closing.
- [Debug Console](https://palbase.studio/docs/ios/debug-console): The in-app debug console: what the SDK and the app record on the device, pb.debug's calls, and the palbase.debug_console flag that opens it for one user.

## Android SDK

- [Overview](https://palbase.studio/docs/android/overview): The Android SDK: the studio.palbase Maven repository and BOM, minSdk 26 and Kotlin 2.2, registering the app, apps:sync and the build step that compiles an environment in, PalbaseClient, and its errors and retries.
- [Auth](https://palbase.studio/docs/android/auth): pb.auth on Android: sign-up and sign-in, guests, second factors, magic links, phone codes, passwords, the observable session bound to the device, signing out and deleting the account.
- [Calling Your Backend](https://palbase.studio/docs/android/backend-calls): The Kotlin client apps:sync generates from your backend's contract: pb.<name>, a typed function per route, its typed errors and BackendError, retries, uploads and a backend on your computer.
- [Gateways](https://palbase.studio/docs/android/gateways): A backend's @Gateway classes from the generated Kotlin client: join, typed events, messages and their acks, PBGatewayError, durable gateways, and a chat gateway's state in Compose.
- [Realtime](https://palbase.studio/docs/android/realtime): pb.realtime channels on Android: broadcasts, a shared state and presence, who may join, and the one socket's connection as a StateFlow.
- [Messaging](https://palbase.studio/docs/android/messaging): palbase-messaging: conversations, timelines and threads as StateFlows, an outbox that sends once, incoming for the app's own banner, pushes that bring a message onto the phone while the app is closed, and FLAG_SECURE for what is seen once.
- [Flags](https://palbase.studio/docs/android/flags): pb.flags on Android: values read without waiting from what the device kept, typed reads, Compose state, per-user values, and live updates over the socket.
- [Analytics](https://palbase.studio/docs/android/analytics): pb.analytics on Android: events, screens, timings and diagnostics, each behind its consent category, batched and kept on the device until sent.
- [Notifications](https://palbase.studio/docs/android/notifications): FCM push on Android: the project's FCM provider, pb.notify.register for the signed-in user, showing the data message a push arrives as, preferences and topics.
- [Storage](https://palbase.studio/docs/android/storage): pb.storage on Android: uploading and downloading through URLs your backend signed, and reading public buckets.
- [Purchases](https://palbase.studio/docs/android/purchases): pb.purchases on Android: what the customer has in any store, kept current, and buying on Google Play with Play Billing: products, purchase, plan changes, restore and web purchase links.
- [Voice](https://palbase.studio/docs/android/voice): PBVoice: a chat's live voice over WebRTC on Android, its offer through your backend, the microphone permission, the device's audio, mute and close.
- [Debug Console](https://palbase.studio/docs/android/debug-console): What the Android SDK records on the device from launch, what the app adds to it, and PalbaseConsole: the in-app console the project opens for one user with a flag.

## Server SDK

- [Overview](https://palbase.studio/docs/server/overview): palbase/server — createServer with the project's secret key: every module's server calls, refusals as PalbaseError, retries and paging.
- [Webhooks](https://palbase.studio/docs/server/webhooks): The project's events delivered to your server: Palbase-Signature, verifyWebhook, and delivery that may come twice but never not at all.

## Auth

- [Overview](https://palbase.studio/docs/auth/overview): An environment's auth, set up from Studio, the CLI or the admin calls: passwords, email confirmation, email links, sessions and token lifetimes, passkeys, risk, security emails, signing keys and auth's own emails.
- [Sign-in Providers](https://palbase.studio/docs/auth/providers): Turning on email, phone, Google, Apple, GitHub and Microsoft sign-in — each provider's clients, secrets and callback URL — and guest accounts.
- [Users & Roles](https://palbase.studio/docs/auth/users): The environment's users: finding, creating, banning, signing out, deleting and exporting them; their sessions; application roles; and importing users with their passwords and sessions.
- [Blocking Hooks](https://palbase.studio/docs/auth/hooks): An endpoint of yours that auth calls and waits for before a sign-up, a sign-in or a token: the events, the signed request and answer, timeouts and failure modes.
- [Audit Trail](https://palbase.studio/docs/auth/audit): Who did what in an environment's auth — sign-ins, changes to users and settings, admin actions — read, exported as JSON lines or CSV, and verified as an unbroken chain.
- [OpenID Provider](https://palbase.studio/docs/auth/openid-provider): Other apps signing in with your users' accounts through the environment's OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect provider, service accounts for machines, and sign-in tokens your own server makes.

## Purchases

- [Overview](https://palbase.studio/docs/purchases/overview): One catalog sold in the App Store, on Google Play and on the web through your Stripe account, and one answer to what each customer has: products, plans, entitlements, credits, limits, the stores and test purchases.
- [Catalog](https://palbase.studio/docs/purchases/catalog): The catalog as a JSON document in revisions: products, plans, prices, channels and what each gives; purchases:catalog:get, validate and put, and the plan that writes it to Stripe, App Store Connect and Google Play once confirmed.
- [App Store](https://palbase.studio/docs/purchases/app-store): Selling in the App Store: the App Store Connect API key and the In-App Purchase key, server notifications, purchases:doctor, and how each StoreKit transaction is verified, owned, restored and refunded.
- [Test Apple Purchases](https://palbase.studio/docs/purchases/testing-apple): Buying the catalog's iOS products before anyone pays: in Xcode from a StoreKit file made from the catalog, then in the App Store sandbox with a tester — and the app's and the server's code for both.
- [Google Play](https://palbase.studio/docs/purchases/google-play): Selling on Google Play: the service account your Play Console invites, the real-time developer notifications topic, and how each Play purchase is read, owned, acknowledged and refunded.
- [Connect Stripe](https://palbase.studio/docs/purchases/connect-stripe): The environment's own Stripe account sells the catalog on the web: connected with one click through Palbase's Stripe App, or with a restricted key.
- [Web](https://palbase.studio/docs/purchases/web): Selling on the web with pb.purchases: offerings, Stripe Checkout, buyers with no account and their redemption links, what the customer has, the customer portal, a paywall in the page, and web checkout from an iOS app.
- [Paywalls](https://palbase.studio/docs/purchases/paywalls): Paywalls designed once and drawn natively, published without an app update: the definition, drafts and versions, assets, placements and their targeting rules, and experiments that say which sells best.
- [Offers & Coupons](https://palbase.studio/docs/purchases/offers): Discounts, free trials and grants for an audience or everyone, once a customer, sold as each store's own offer; and coupons: shared or one-time codes, and App Store offer codes.
- [Entitlements, Credits & Limits](https://palbase.studio/docs/purchases/entitlements): CustomerInfo and isEntitled on your server; credits spent in one step or held with withReservation; quotas in windows with overflow; and the purchases events your backend receives.
- [Customers](https://palbase.studio/docs/purchases/customers): Looking a customer up, giving and revoking entitlements, guests whose purchases move to the account they sign in to, restores, deleted users, and the purchase settings.
- [Charts](https://palbase.studio/docs/purchases/charts): Revenue, MRR, subscriptions, conversion, LTV and retention from the ledger: purchases:charts, segments and filters, revenue types, CSV, and the reporting currency and fees.

## Messaging

- [Overview](https://palbase.studio/docs/messaging/overview): Chat between a project's people: direct conversations and groups, threads, files, timers, seen once, vanish mode; history that belongs to the account, encrypted per conversation; pushes, screenshots, your server's reads, moderation, settings and prices.

## Analytics

- [Overview](https://palbase.studio/docs/analytics/overview): What a project's analytics keeps — events, people, performance samples, request traces, console history — whose each one is, consent, how long it is kept, and its limits.
- [Reading Analytics](https://palbase.studio/docs/analytics/reading): Studio's Analytics screens, and the secret key's reads: summaries, event lists and timelines, breakdowns, funnels and retention, from a server or the CLI.
- [Performance](https://palbase.studio/docs/analytics/performance): Web vitals, app starts, network and custom samples; the requests your apps and backend report; and a device's debug history — in Studio and from a server.

## Client Apps

- [Client Apps](https://palbase.studio/docs/apps/overview): Registering a project's iOS, Android and web apps with the CLI: what each is in an environment, its own publishable key, the passkey association files the environment publishes from it, and deleting and restoring one.
- [Syncing an App's Settings](https://palbase.studio/docs/apps/sync): What palbase apps:sync writes under palbase/ in an app's repository — each environment's settings, its publishable key and its backends' typed clients — how a build picks its environment, and checking it in CI.

## App Distribution

- [App Distribution](https://palbase.studio/docs/distribution/overview): Builds from your build machine to TestFlight and Google Play's internal testing: packages and build numbers, deliveries and their states, the actions a person confirms, Studio's screens and the stores events.
- [TestFlight](https://palbase.studio/docs/distribution/testflight): An iOS app's builds to TestFlight with your own Apple account: connecting an App Store Connect key, the unsigned .ipa and its entitlements, signing, groups and testers, Beta App Review and export compliance.
- [App Store](https://palbase.studio/docs/distribution/app-store): An iOS app's App Store page and the version App Review gets: the draft page and its screenshots, planned and confirmed; preparing the version, what is missing, sending it to App Review, releasing it, the phased release, and App Review's answer.
- [Google Play](https://palbase.studio/docs/distribution/google-play): An Android app's builds to Google Play's internal testing: the service account Play Console invites, the upload key Palbase signs with, the .aab and its version code, and the first release made in Play Console.
- [App Health](https://palbase.studio/docs/distribution/health): Each linked app in its store: the App Store Connect webhook Palbase makes and the key role it needs, the events it tells and their source, testers' crashes and screenshots, the App Store's crash data and Play's vitals, and Play's releases read every 10 minutes.

## Machines & Databases

- [Machines](https://palbase.studio/docs/machines/overview): Your own code on Palbase: a machine's size, sleep and wake, its address and port, health check, copies, environment, secrets, crons and tasks.
- [Connecting GitHub](https://palbase.studio/docs/machines/github): The Palbase Cloud GitHub App, a machine's repository, branch and directory, and which pushes build which machines.
- [Builds, Logs & Rollback](https://palbase.studio/docs/machines/builds): What a push does: the build, the settings .env.example asks for, the rollout beside what serves, the logs, and returning to an earlier build.
- [Databases](https://palbase.studio/docs/machines/databases): Postgres of your own: sizes, the passwords shown once, the owner and app logins, direct and pooled addresses, who may connect, a machine's database, and the SQL console.
- [Backups & Restore](https://palbase.studio/docs/machines/backups): Backups kept for the days you choose, bringing a database back to a moment, and deleting, taking back and purging one.

## Optional

- [The whole corpus in one file](https://palbase.studio/llms-full.txt): every section in one file.
- [Backend only](https://palbase.studio/llms-backend.txt): getting-started + backend + server + machines, the slice for writing a Palbase backend and putting it on a machine.
- Any page as raw Markdown: replace `/docs/` with `/docs-md/`, or append `.md` to its URL.
